newsitem.title: USA: Navistar in venture to make Paystar truck.
newsitem.headline: Navistar in venture to make Paystar truck.

text.p: Navistar International Corp said Friday it entered a joint venture with TIC United Corp to produce Navistar's Paystar heavy-duty trucks.
TIC, based in Dallas, makes steel castings and forgings, fabricated metal products and agriculture/transportation equipment. It is also involved in bulk transportation.
Navistar said it will have 34 percent of the venture, with TIC controlling 51 percent. The venture's management will hold 15 percent. Other terms were not disclosed.
The Paystar will be made at the joint venture's Garland, Texas, plant in starting in early 1997.
The Garland plant is now owned by TIC.

The Paystar heavy-duty, severe-service truck line is geared for on- and off-highway markets, including construction, coal hauling, and oil field. These trucks are currently produced at Navistar's Chatham, Ontario, assembly plant.

"The joint venture will help us achieve greater efficiencies at our Chatham assembly operations as we focus those operations on producing only heavy-duty conventional trucks," John Horne, Navistar chairman, said in a statement.
"Severe service trucks by nature of their applications are highly complex and, therefore, are best assembled at a facility where they are the only trucks produced," he added.

Navistar said the joint venture is a key part of its strategy to be more competitive by focusing its assembly plants on producing trucks with less variation from model to model. At Chatham, the company intends to produce only the International 9000 series of heavy-duty trucks.
The company said it will introduce the International 9100 series truck, an addition to the heavy-duty truck line produced at Chatham.

The International 9100 truck is designed for local and regional operators, with applications including beverage, refrigeration, less than truck load (LTL), hub-and-spoke freight pickup and general freight delivery.
Any changes in employment at Chatham, if required, will be determined based on the transition of the Paystar, the production schedule for the International 9100 and market demand for both trucks.
Navistar said it is also phasing down production of its International 8200 heavy-duty truck model, currently produced at its Springfield, Ohio, plant.

"We are taking this step to begin to focus the Springfield assembly plant on producing only medium-duty trucks," Horne said. "We will continue to offer customers a comprehensive range of selections to meet their applications and operating needs, including choices like the International 9100 truck."

Navistar will take orders for the International 8200 through January 1997 and will continue production through mid-year. Its dealer network will continue to provide service and parts for the International 8200 trucks, it added.
Based on current market conditions and production schedules, no layoffs are anticipated at Springfield.
